svg.title: Thirty Days to a Documented Operating System
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-first-thirty-days-operating-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Thirty Days to a Documented Operating System; subtitle: Build sourcing, underwriting, closing controls, and payment evidence before scaling.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Four milestone values are ending calendar days: 7, 14, 21, and 30. This sprint prepares the operation; the canonical first-deal expectation remains 2–6 months. Do not force a closing into thirty days to satisfy the diagram.; caption: Day 30 success means an auditable acquisition and servicing process with named owners, funded operating runway, and a qualified pipeline—not an assumed funded transaction.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Select the market and document statutory operating requirements; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Owner and counsel choose one jurisdiction, review 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3 and applicable state wrap rules, engage the RMLO, and map title, disclosure, and servicing responsibilities. Deliver a written transaction checklist and startup cash allocation.; label: Days 8-14; value: Configure sourcing records and rehearse the underwriting workflow; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Build the deduplicated seller cohort, configure CRM stage definitions, and assemble an authorized sample file. Test senior-debt amortization, wrap amortization, escrow changes, default carrying cost, and acceleration liquidity in a spreadsheet.; label: Days 15-21; value: Validate buyer qualification and licensed-servicer payment controls; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Have the RMLO review a qualified buyer file when available; otherwise rehearse with clearly synthetic records. Confirm servicer licensing and contractual scope, test reconciliation exports without live funds, and rehearse a failed underlying payment escalation.; label: Days 22-30; value: Review qualified files and prove end-to-end exception handling; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Counsel reviews candidate documents and notice timing; operations completes a mock monthly reconciliation. The owner verifies runway and deal-specific liquidity, records unresolved defects, and schedules only files that satisfy the documented requirements.

text.title: Thirty Days to a Documented Operating System
text.tspan: Thirty Days to a Documented Operating System

rect.title: label: Days 1-7; value: Select the market and document statutory operating requirements; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Owner and counsel choose one jurisdiction, review 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3 and applicable state wrap rules, engage the RMLO, and map title, disclosure, and servicing responsibilities. Deliver a written transaction checklist and startup cash allocation.

text.title: Select the market and document statutory operating requirements

rect.title: label: Days 8-14; value: Configure sourcing records and rehearse the underwriting workflow; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Build the deduplicated seller cohort, configure CRM stage definitions, and assemble an authorized sample file. Test senior-debt amortization, wrap amortization, escrow changes, default carrying cost, and acceleration liquidity in a spreadsheet.

text.title: Configure sourcing records and rehearse the underwriting workflow

rect.title: label: Days 15-21; value: Validate buyer qualification and licensed-servicer payment controls; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Have the RMLO review a qualified buyer file when available; otherwise rehearse with clearly synthetic records. Confirm servicer licensing and contractual scope, test reconciliation exports without live funds, and rehearse a failed underlying payment escalation.

text.title: Validate buyer qualification and licensed-servicer payment controls

rect.title: label: Days 22-30; value: Review qualified files and prove end-to-end exception handling; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Counsel reviews candidate documents and notice timing; operations completes a mock monthly reconciliation. The owner verifies runway and deal-specific liquidity, records unresolved defects, and schedules only files that satisfy the documented requirements.
